specification.name: RetinaGuard Vision Suite
specification.description:
RetinaGuard Vision Suite is a medium-scale, monolithic C application designed to detect, grade, and longitudinally track diabetic retinopathy from retinal fundus photographs captured in primary-care clinics. The single executable orchestrates the full computer-vision pipeline—from image ingestion and quality control to model inference, result visualization, and automated feedback to electronic medical-record (EMR) systems—inside a tightly coupled codebase. The healthcare focus is reinforced through domain-specific feature engineering (e.g., micro-aneurysm heat-maps), risk-stratified model evaluation reports aligned with ophthalmology guidelines, and outcomes monitoring that triggers clinician alerts when disease progression is detected.

Built around a monolithic architecture, RetinaGuard embeds Observer Pattern hooks to broadcast inference events to an in-process model-registry module and a real-time monitoring dashboard. The Pipeline Pattern stitches together discrete stages—image preprocessing, feature extraction, model serving, evaluation, and visualization—while remaining in one deployable unit that can be certified as a single medical device software component. MLOps functionality (hyperparameter tuning, automated retraining, and model versioning) is performed on-device at scheduled intervals using historic images stored in an internal database, ensuring data never leaves the clinic and simplifying regulatory compliance for protected health information (PHI). This design produces a reliable, self-contained solution that rural and resource-limited clinics can operate without cloud connectivity or complex distributed infrastructure.
dependencies: OpenCV 4.x (core image processing and computer vision)
LibTorch C++ API 2.x (deep-learning inference and training)
SQLite3 (embedded model registry, data cache, and audit logs)
libcurl (secure EMR integration via HL7/FHIR REST endpoints)
Cairo Graphics (in-app heat-map and ROC curve visualization)
Systemd Service Files / pkg-config (Linux packaging and deployment)
